notes.claim: With an unchanging flux there is no induced emf in the loop and no current from it.
A sinusoidal supply voltage on a coil is tied by a definite relation to the flux density in the core and the core's size.
Transformers cannot change DC voltages, because they work by Faraday's law of induction.

sources.title: 5.1: Magnetic Induction - Physics LibreTexts
sources.quote: With an unchanging flux, there is no induced emf in the loop, and no current as a result.

sources.title: Chapter 5
sources.quote: This equation demonstrates a definite relation between the voltage in a coil, the flux density, and the size of the core.

sources.title: 23.10: Transformers - Physics LibreTexts
sources.quote: The fact that transformers are based on Faraday’s law of induction makes it clear why we cannot use transformers to change DC voltages.
